run.market_summary: 1) Hawkish rates shock. October CPI came in hot at +0.4%, Fed officials are openly talking about a 50bp hike, and Goldman has changed its Fed forecast. The 10-year Treasury yield is above 5%, and yields had their biggest jump since the tariff selloff. This is the strongest, highest-volume signal (monetary policy +0.72, inflation +0.67), and it is the only theme I'm trading. 2) AI and semiconductor stress. Investigations into Nvidia's China exports have already knocked NVDA down 18% in five days. The headlines are specific to Nvidia, and most of the move has already happened, so there is little left to trade. CoreWeave's earnings 'AI revival' did not hold (CRWV is down 9%). 3) Oil and geopolitics are noise right now. The Iran–Hormuz headlines are being offset by OPEC+ output increases and a smaller war premium. The energy-supply score is near zero and XLE is down 6.7%. Overall: express the rates view through the cleanest instruments (dollar, long bonds, rate-sensitive small caps), keep sizes moderate because a single CPI print can fade and a 5% 10-year tends to attract buyers, and don't chase the chip names after their drop.

ideas.thesis: This is the cleanest way to trade the hawkish repricing. 'Dollar firms as hot inflation, hawkish Fed talk lift rate-hike bets', and talk of a possible 50bp hike widens the US rate advantage over other countries. It is only up 0.5% over five days, so most of the move probably hasn't happened yet.

Hot CPI (+0.4%) plus Fed officials opening the door to a 50bp hike puts pressure on long bonds, and the 10-year is above 5%. TLT is down only 0.3% over five days, which looks too small given the size of the yield-spike headlines.

Small caps are the most rate-sensitive part of the equity market because they carry more floating-rate debt and are more exposed to credit. Yet IWM is up 0.3% over five days while hike odds have jumped. I prefer it over SPY or QQQ as the single equity short on the rates theme.

analysis.headline: Chips led the market higher after CoreWeave's results revived the AI trade. Semis (SMH +4.8%) and the Nasdaq (+2.3%) gained mostly in the opening gap. Rates went nowhere after Tuesday's hot-CPI shock, while the dollar kept climbing on Fed hike bets.
analysis.narrative:
Only one move was truly unusual: the dollar (UUP +0.69%, z +2.0), which extended Tuesday's CPI-driven rally to what headlines called a 19-month high in the dollar index. Everything else was within about 1.2 standard deviations, because the last 20 sessions have been very volatile (headlines say the SOX index fell 21% in a month). So the big percentage gains in chips were large but not abnormal for this period: SMH +4.8%, AMD +7.3%, INTC +7.5%, LRCX/AMAT +6%. Almost all of it came in the gap: SMH gapped up 4.4%, XLK 2.9% and QQQ 1.85%, with only about 0.4% added during the session. That points to overnight news, and the news was CoreWeave's Q3 report after Tuesday's close. Per Reuters, CoreWeave raised its revenue forecast and signaled it would borrow less, which eased worries about an AI debt bubble. CRWV closed up about 25%, Nvidia rebounded (+2.9%, down from about +5% premarket) despite the Huang probe and a downgrade, and suppliers rallied together. AMD had its own catalysts on top: a $2.5B Anthropic stake, a Goldman top-pick call, and EPYC Venice chips starting to ship. AMAT/LRCX/KLA also rallied ahead of AMAT's earnings.

The rally was narrow under the surface. The cloud spenders fell steadily after opening higher: MSFT -2.3% (-2.45% from the open), AMZN -1.7% and META -2.0% (each down about 2.6–2.8% from the open). Money appears to have rotated from the companies paying for AI capex into the companies selling to them. AAPL (+2.0%, a record high, after an analyst upgrade and a UBS note on iPhone shortages) and GOOGL (+2.1%) went the other way. Outside tech the moves were ordinary: DIA +0.5%, IWM +0.9% (all in the gap), defensives flat to slightly up, and 11 of 13 sectors higher. VIX fell 10%, mostly during the session.

Rates did not follow through. The 10-year rose 2bp to 5.00% and TLT was flat. Nov 11 is Veterans Day, so the cash Treasury market was likely closed or thin, which makes the yield readings less informative. The hike repricing showed up instead in the dollar and in gold (-1.0%, all of it after the open). China moved against the global rally: FXI -1.4% and KWEB -1.6% on 2.2x volume. Hong Kong retreated as high US rates weighed, per BigGo. EEM still rose 2.4%, which likely reflects its Taiwan and Korea chip weighting (TSMC about +4%, SK hynix higher). Energy rose (XLE +1.9%) even though crude was flat (+0.45%), a normal-sized move without a clear cause. Iran's strike on an Omani island is the only supply headline.

For tomorrow: AI-capex sentiment, not the Fed, set equity direction today. The hawkish shock remains live in FX and gold but has stopped spreading to equities for now. Watch whether the 5% 10-year holds when the cash market is fully open.

analysis.cross_asset_read: Equities up, VIX down 10%, tech and semis leading: a risk-on day driven by one sector. The stronger dollar (z +2) and weaker gold show the hawkish Fed repricing still working through FX and precious metals. Yields were flat, though Veterans Day likely kept the cash Treasury market closed or thin, so equities were not responding to rates today. Chips up while the cloud spenders fell intraday looks like rotation within AI, not a broad tech bid. EEM up while FXI/KWEB fell shows the EM gain was a chip trade through Taiwan and Korea, not EM risk appetite. Energy outperformed while crude was flat, which is not explained.

axis_realized.note: No new Fed news today, but the hike repricing from Tuesday's CPI carried on through the dollar (UUP z +2.0) and gold (-1%). Yields were flat on a likely thin or closed cash bond market, and equities ignored it.

model_grade.summary: The model built its day around a hawkish rates shock that was already priced on Tuesday, and it missed the main story: CoreWeave's results reviving AI and semis. It dismissed CoreWeave based on an after-hours drop that fully reversed (CRWV closed about +25%). Only the dollar call worked. Short IWM lost money, short TLT was flat, and 'don't chase chips' missed a 4.8% SMH move.
got_right: LONG UUP: +0.69% (the session's only z>1.5 move), confirming hike bets still drive FX
Hawkish tone still mattered for gold (-1%) and Hong Kong/China tech
Its warning that a 5% 10-year tends to attract buyers was right: yields did not extend
got_wrong: Called CoreWeave's 'AI revival' a failure (CRWV -9%). CRWV actually rallied about 25% and drove the whole tape
'Don't chase the chip names': SMH +4.8%, AMD +7.3%, INTC +7.5%
SHORT IWM: IWM +0.89%. A rates-based short does not work when yields are flat
SHORT TLT: flat, with no follow-through in yields

lessons: Score a theme on whether it will move prices from here, not on how many headlines it has. A CPI shock the day before, already reflected in yields and the dollar, should be scored lower for trading the next day.
Check premarket prices for overnight earnings reactions before forming a view. The after-hours CRWV drop the model cited had reversed into a premarket rally by the time it ran (13:06 UTC).
Add a market-calendar check: on bond-market holidays (Veterans Day, Columbus Day), reduce weight on TLT/TNX/IWM rate-expression trades.
Require price confirmation for policy headlines in oversold sectors. Export-control headlines after a 21% one-month SOX drop did not push chips lower.
Only pair small-cap shorts with a rates view when yields are actually rising that morning. Otherwise IWM follows broad risk appetite.
